title: Shakti as a philosophy
hook: earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, the sense of I: in the Gita, Krishna calls the whole list his nature, and then says there's more

segments.voice: Yesterday, Shakti as a philosophy in the Shvetashvatara Upanishad: seekers set down their list of answers, sat, and saw God's own power hidden in its own qualities. Whose hidden hand did you notice? Day one thousand eighty-five, and the end of a week.

Earth. Water. Fire. Air. Space. Mind. Intellect. The sense of I. In the seventh chapter of the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna lists these, one after another, the way you'd unpack a box onto a table. The ground under your feet, the water in your glass, the thoughts in your head, even the feeling of being someone: all of it on one list. And then he says something about the list. This is my nature, he says. Mine. Divided this way. And then, before Arjuna can take that in, he adds: and this is the lower one. There's another. Today, at the end of a week on Shakti as a philosophy, the Gita's map of the power that holds the world.
screen: `EARTH, WATER, FIRE, AIR, SPACE.` → `MIND, INTELLECT, THE SENSE OF I.` → `THIS IS MY NATURE. THE LOWER ONE.`

segments.voice: Here are the verses, in paraphrase. Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and the sense of I: this is my prakriti, my nature, divided eightfold. That is the lower. Know my other, higher nature, the life in things, by which this whole world is upheld. All beings come from these two, as from a womb. I am where the whole world begins, and where it dissolves. First, notice the word. Prakriti: nature, the stuff and the shaping of things. Krishna calls it his. Matter isn't the enemy of the divine here. It belongs to God. Second, notice what's on the lower list. Not only rocks and rivers. Mind, intellect and the sense of I are there too. The thoughts you're thinking right now are, in the Gita's picture, part of nature, part of the lower prakriti. Third, the higher nature: the life itself, the one that holds the world up. Some readers hear in it every living being; others hear the very spark of awareness in each one. Either way, the world doesn't just sit there. It's held. Fourth, the week. Here the Gita speaks through Krishna; in the days ahead, a goddess text will take up this same word, prakriti, in her own voice. Look back at the road here. Parvati, tested in the forest by a visitor in disguise, and Parvati feeding Shiva in Kashi. Ramakrishna's snake, still or moving. A verse where Shiva can't stir without Shakti. A blade of grass that fire and wind couldn't move, and Uma who named the power behind them. Seekers who saw God's own power hidden in the world. And now the Gita, putting earth and mind and the sense of I on one list, and saying: all of this is mine, and there is more.
screen: `PRAKRITI: MY NATURE, EIGHTFOLD.` · `EVEN MIND AND THE SENSE OF I.` · `THE HIGHER NATURE HOLDS THE WORLD UP.` · `THE WEEK: A VERSE, A STRAW, A SEEING.` · then, large: `ALL OF THIS IS MINE, AND THERE IS MORE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: walk the list. Sit, and let the breath settle. Then go through Krishna's list slowly, one at a time. Earth: the weight of you on the chair or the floor. Water: the wet of the mouth. Fire: the warmth of the hands. Air: the breath. Space: the room around you. Mind: the next thought, arriving. Intellect: the part that names it. The sense of I: the feeling that this is all happening to someone. Then stop listing, and rest in whatever is aware of the whole list. If you pray, you can offer the list back in the words you use. The bell holds the time.
Shakti as a philosophy. In the Gita, earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and the sense of I make up the lower nature, and a higher one holds the world up.
Your line: Shakti as a philosophy. Today, the next time you feel your own mind racing, say quietly: this is nature too. Day one thousand eighty-five. A week walked.

howItsDone: The Bhagavad Gita's seventh chapter is studied and chanted in homes and Gita classes, and teachers use its two natures, lower and higher, to explain how the divine relates to the world.

fork.setup: you're Arjuna. Krishna lists earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect and the sense of I, and calls it all his nature. what does he say next?
options: that this is everything there is.
that this is the lower nature, and he has a higher one.
that only the mind is real.
fork.reveal: this is the lower, he says. know my other, higher nature, the life by which this world is upheld.

original.note: Sanskrit: prakriti, nature. In the Gita, Krishna calls his nature lower and higher.

trapdoor: what you thought: nature is rocks and rivers, and the mind is something else.
what it means: in the Gita, earth and mind and the sense of I are all one nature, the lower one, and a higher nature holds the world up.

'Goddess traditions take up this same word, prakriti, and give it a face' is a general claim pointing ahead to the Devi Upanishad (day 1087). Keeper to confirm the phrasing.
